pointers.sentence: The session middleware makes a store for every request, used or not (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_request`), and a store reads nothing until its data is used.

`SessionBase.__init__` keeps the key it is given, if it is valid, sets both flags false and imports the serializer `SESSION_SERIALIZER` names; it reads nothing (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.__init__`).

Otherwise it fills it, once: with an empty dictionary when the store has no key or the caller passes `no_load=True`, as a backend's save does when told to create the session, and else with what the backend's `SessionBase.load` returns (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._get_session`).

`SessionBase.modified` is set by what changes the dictionary: `__setitem__`, `SessionBase.update` and `clear` always, `__delitem__` and `SessionBase.pop` only when the key was there, `SessionBase.setdefault` only when it sets (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.pop`); a backend's `SessionBase.create` sets it too.
The documentation says to set it by hand (`docs/topics/http/sessions.txt`).
`SessionBase.is_empty` is true when the store has no key and its data is empty or was never loaded (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.is_empty`).
`SessionBase.__bool__` is new (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

The store's own code assigns `SessionBase._session_key`, a second property over the same value whose setter stores `None` in place of a value that `SessionBase._validate_session_key` refuses (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._set_session_key`).

A new key is 32 characters that `get_random_string` draws from `VALID_KEY_CHARS`, the lower-case letters and the digits, drawn again for as long as `SessionBase.exists` says the key is taken (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._get_new_session_key`).

`SessionBase.encode` turns the dictionary into a string with `dumps`, the store's serializer and the salt `SessionBase.key_salt`; `SessionBase.decode` reads it back with `loads` (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.encode`).

Only the database, cached-database and file backends store what `encode` makes; the cache backend hands the cache the dictionary itself, and the signed-cookie backend signs with a salt of its own (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/cache.py:SessionStore.save`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/signed_cookies.py:SessionStore._get_session_key`).

Only the database, cached-database and file backends store what `encode` makes; the cache backend hands the cache the dictionary itself, and the signed-cookie backend signs with a salt of its own (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/cache.py:SessionStore.save`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/signed_cookies.py:SessionStore._get_session_key`).

On `BadSignature` it logs `"Session data corrupted"` as a warning to `"django.security.SuspiciousSession"` and returns an empty dictionary; on any other exception it returns one silently, a comment naming `ValueError` and unpickling errors (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.decode`).
`SESSION_SERIALIZER` names `django.contrib.sessions.serializers.JSONSerializer` by default, the signing module's `JSONSerializer` under another name (`django/contrib/sessions/serializers.py`).
`SessionBase.set_expiry` keeps the session's own expiry in its data, under `"_session_expiry"` (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.set_expiry`).

`SessionBase.get_expiry_age` answers in seconds from now and `SessionBase.get_expiry_date` as a moment: no entry, or 0, means `SESSION_COOKIE_AGE`; an integer, that many seconds; a string, the moment it names (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.get_expiry_age`).

`SessionBase.clear` puts an empty dictionary in place of the data without loading the old, which a comment calls wasted time, and sets both flags; the key stays, so a save writes an empty session under it (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.clear`).

`SessionBase.cycle_key` loads the data, has the backend `create` a session under a new key, puts the data back, and deletes what was stored under the old key (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.cycle_key`).

`save` with `must_create=True` must create a stored session or raise `CreateError`, which `create` catches to try another key; otherwise it must only update one or raise `UpdateError`, which the middleware raises again as `SessionInterrupted` (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.save`, [The session backends](session-backends.md)).
The test cookie methods store `"worked"` under `"testcookie"`, for a later request to check that the browser keeps cookies (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.set_test_cookie`).

A twin reaches the data through `SessionBase._aget_session`: the steps of `_get_session`, with `SessionBase.aload` awaited in place of `load` (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._aget_session`).
